Film and television location documentation.

Production Documentation

Production teams make expensive decisions based on location photographs that don't tell the whole story. Alturascope provides navigable 3D documentation of filming locations — giving directors, production designers, and art departments spatial data they can work from before the tech scout, and a timestamped condition record that protects location owners after the crew leaves.

What we document.

Complete interior and exterior documentation. Every room, every access point, every surface. Ceiling heights, structural elements, power and services locations. Pre-production and post-wrap condition records. The documentation captures the spatial reality of the location so your creative team can make decisions remotely and your location team has a complete condition record.

What you receive.

Matterport digital twin navigable by the entire creative team, narrated location walkthrough, labeled photo storyboard by area, and conditions record with timestamped documentation. All delivered through ScopeWalk and permanently accessible to the production team.

Who this is for.

Location managers, production designers, art departments, location owners and agents, and VFX and pre-visualisation teams. Whether you're scouting, planning, or protecting a location — the documentation serves the same purpose: accurate spatial information your team can trust.

How it works.

01

We handle all logistics — building access, security, travel, and scheduling. Travel costs are included in project pricing.

Frequently asked questions.

How is a Matterport location scan used in pre-production? +

The Matterport digital twin gives your production designer, art department, and director a navigable 3D model of the location they can explore remotely — measuring spaces, planning camera positions, and understanding spatial relationships without being on site. This reduces the number of physical scouts required, allows remote collaboration across departments, and gives the entire creative team access to the same spatial reference simultaneously.

How long does a location scan take? +

Most standard location scans take between four and eight hours on site, depending on the size and complexity of the space. Multi-floor or multi-building locations may require a full day. The capture process is non-disruptive and can work around schedules. We scope the duration during the brief and confirm before we arrive.

Can you document exterior locations as well as interiors? +

Yes. We document both interior and exterior environments. For exterior locations, we capture the spatial context, access points, surrounding structures, and conditions. Combined with the interior documentation, this gives your production team a complete picture of the location and its context.

What does post-production location documentation include? +

Post-wrap documentation creates a timestamped condition record of the location after the crew has left. This includes a Matterport digital twin, labeled photographs of every area, and a conditions report documenting the state of the location. This protects both the production company and the location owner by providing an objective record of post-production conditions.

Can the production team navigate the scan remotely before the tech scout? +

Yes. The Matterport digital twin is accessible through any web browser — no special software required. Your entire creative team can navigate the location remotely, take measurements, and plan their approach before setting foot on site. Access is provided through ScopeWalk and can be shared with as many team members as needed.
